advisories.title: Command injection in Hikvision web server
advisories.summary: A crafted request to the device web server can run operating-system commands without authentication, giving full control of the camera.

remediation.action: Install the vendor firmware update for this model
Remove the camera from the public internet — delete any port-forward or UPnP mapping to it
Move the camera to an isolated IoT VLAN or guest network

advisories.title: Authentication bypass in Hikvision cameras
advisories.summary: An improper authentication path allows escalation to administrator and disclosure of device credentials.

remediation.action: Install the vendor firmware update for this model
Rotate every device and stream password after updating
Remove the camera from the public internet

advisories.title: Identity authentication bypass in Dahua devices
advisories.summary: The login process can be bypassed, allowing a remote party to authenticate as a valid device user.

remediation.action: Install the vendor firmware update for this model
Remove the camera from the public internet
Move the camera to an isolated IoT VLAN or guest network

advisories.title: Device may still use factory default credentials
advisories.summary: Many consumer devices ship with a published default username and password. Anyone who can reach the device can look these up.

remediation.action: Set a unique password on the device now
Disable any remote-access account you do not use

advisories.title: Device is reachable from the public internet
advisories.summary: A device reachable from outside your network is exposed to automated internet-wide scanning, which finds and attacks new devices within minutes.

remediation.action: Delete the port-forward rule for this device on your router
Turn off UPnP on your router so devices cannot open their own ports
Use the vendor app or a VPN for remote viewing instead of a port-forward
